text: Hong Kong health authorities are investigating the fourth food poisoning cluster linked to raw oysters reported within a week. Six people, two males and four females aged 29 to 35, fell ill after having dinner at Chef's Cuts restaurant at the Airside mall in Kai Tak. They developed diarrhoea, abdominal pain, vomiting, nausea and fever about 11 to 37 hours after having dinner. This follows three other similar incidents since last Friday linked to raw oyster consumption at different restaurants. The CHP urged residents to avoid eating raw seafood and maintain personal, food, and environmental hygiene.

Hong Kong's health authorities have warned of a recent drastic increase in norovirus-related food poisoning incidents all related to raw oyster consumption, with 20 cases recorded over the past 2½ weeks. The Centre for Health Protection received 23 reports of food poisoning involving 69 patients since January 18. Among them, 20 cases affecting 57 people were related to norovirus, which typically causes food poisoning and acute gastroenteritis. An epidemiological investigation showed all cases were related to raw oyster consumption from origins including Korea, France, Ireland, and Spain. Five patients were hospitalized but their conditions were stable.

The Centre for Health Protection is investigating two related cases involving five individuals, aged between 30 and 38, who dined at Chef's Cuts Restaurant in Wong Chuk Hang on January 30. Symptoms including diarrhoea, abdominal pain, vomiting, and fever manifested between 14 to 49 hours after the meal. Earlier this week, six individuals fell ill after eating oysters at another Chef's Cuts branch. In response, food safety authorities ordered suppliers to cease oyster sales immediately. The number of food poisoning incidents has surged from about one per week in late December to 27 cases in the first week of February.

A one-year-old girl may have suffered food poisoning after consuming Nestlé infant milk formula, Hong Kong authorities have said. The Centre for Food Safety ordered the immediate removal of 390 cans of Aptamil Profutura DUO Advance 1 from shelves, expanding a citywide recall to include a second batch imported from Germany. The scare centres on the possible presence of cereulide, a toxin produced by Bacillus cereus, in baby milk formula. The girl suffered diarrhoea up to five times a day after consuming the formula. The health authorities cannot rule out cereulide poisoning from the powdered infant formula.

Researchers have discovered that people with a specific genetic mutation in the ISG15 protein can fight off virtually any virus without showing symptoms. This discovery has led to the development of a drug inspired by the mutation that could potentially be a universal antiviral effective against every virus. In summer 2025, researchers published results of experiments where mice and hamsters were given a drug inspired by the ISG15 deficiency. When exposed to influenza and SARS-CoV-2, neither virus was able to replicate or cause severe symptoms. This represents breakthrough research in broad-spectrum antiviral drug development.

Hong Kong's Centre for Health Protection has reported a surge in influenza A (H3N2) cases linked to a Hong Kong strain that has spread globally. Kazakhstan, Vietnam, and Japan are facing severe outbreaks during the 2025-2026 flu season. The strain originated from Hong Kong and has caused increased hospitalizations and deaths across multiple countries. Health authorities are monitoring the situation closely and have issued warnings about the highly contagious nature of the strain. Vaccination campaigns have been intensified in affected regions.

Airport health authorities across Asia have stepped up screening measures after India confirmed two Nipah virus infections. Thailand and Malaysia have increased health checks at airports, particularly for passengers arriving from India. A Hong Kong airport authority spokesperson confirmed enhanced health screening measures are being enforced by the health department, including temperature checks at gates for passengers arriving from India. Nipah virus has a high mortality rate and has caused outbreaks in Asia in previous years, triggering concern among public health officials.

In 2025, medicine saw major advances despite political challenges. A landmark case involved a 6-month-old baby whose liver cells were edited using CRISPR technology to correct a unique mutation, allowing the child to resume a normal diet and avoid a liver transplant. Additionally, the year marked significant progress in the war on HIV with new treatments. The medical system is adapting to make such individualized gene therapies more accessible, representing breakthrough developments in genetic medicine and infectious disease treatment.

Studies show that public response to disease outbreaks varies significantly based on perceived severity and media coverage. Research found that there was a much stronger public response to the SARS outbreak in Hong Kong than to the H1N1 swine flu, even though the infection rate in the swine flu outbreak was hundreds of times greater. Public health campaigns and clear communication from authorities influence compliance with preventive measures. Social media plays an increasingly important role in shaping public perception and behaviour during disease outbreaks.

Hong Kong has implemented comprehensive measures to achieve and sustain measles elimination, including high coverage of two-dose measles-containing vaccine, catch-up campaigns, and supplementary immunisation activities. The success story demonstrates the importance of comprehensive surveillance systems and outbreak preparation. Recent travel advisories warn against taking children under one year to areas with measles outbreaks, as they are not yet due for MMR vaccination under the Hong Kong Childhood Immunisation Programme and remain susceptible to infection.

Hong Kong has extended subsidies for the 2025/26 flu vaccine to chronic disease patients aged 18-49, expanding access to vaccination. The government continues to promote flu vaccination as a key public health measure to prevent seasonal influenza outbreaks. Health authorities have emphasized the importance of early vaccination, especially for high-risk groups. The subsidy extension aims to increase vaccination rates and reduce the burden on healthcare systems during flu season.

The US CDC reports that influenza contributed to 1.5% of deaths during the week ending January 24, 2026, with flu activity continuing to surge across the country. Emergency departments are seeing high numbers of flu patients with severe symptoms including very high fever, loss of appetite, trouble breathing, and inability to keep fluids down. Health officials are urging high-risk individuals to seek medical attention promptly. The 2025-2026 flu season has already broken last season's records for cases and hospitalizations.

Research has shown that antiviral drugs such as nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and molnupiravir are effective in preventing severe and fatal COVID-19 outcomes in Hong Kong. A real-world study compared the effectiveness of SARS-CoV-2 oral antiviral drugs and vaccinations, examining their interaction effects. Hospitalized COVID-19 patients who received nirmatrelvir/ritonavir had significantly lower all-cause mortality and disease progression risks than those receiving molnupiravir. These findings support the continued use and development of antiviral therapies for communicable diseases.

A comprehensive study examined adverse events associated with COVID-19 vaccines in Hong Kong, analyzing the relationship between vaccination and adverse events of special interest among patients with chronic disease. The research aimed to examine potential additional risks following vaccination associated with multimorbidity. Despite vaccine hesitancy due to fear of adverse reactions, the study provides important data on vaccine safety. Public health officials continue to emphasize the benefits of vaccination outweigh the risks for most populations.

During the SARS outbreak in Hong Kong, almost 60% of nosocomial acquisition occurred among healthcare workers, highlighting the critical importance of proactive infection control measures. Hong Kong has developed detailed response systems with different guidelines and protocols for various outbreak levels. The six areas addressed during outbreaks include enhancing organizational structure, immigration control, minimizing community spread, promoting personal hygiene, improving anti-epidemic facilities, and resource allocation. These lessons have shaped Hong Kong's preparedness for future disease outbreaks.

Hong Kong authorities have stepped up health screening measures at the airport amid concerns about a mystery disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo that has killed at least 79 people. The Centre for Health Protection is facilitating enhanced health screening for all flights arriving from African transit hubs. This proactive approach reflects lessons learned from past outbreaks including SARS and COVID-19. The government is taking precautionary measures to prevent the importation of any unidentified disease into Hong Kong.

The WHO reported a major chikungunya outbreak in China, with 16,452 locally transmitted cases reported in Guangdong Province as of September 2025. This represents the largest documented chikungunya outbreak to date in China. While Hong Kong has not reported local transmission, health authorities remain vigilant given the proximity to affected areas. Travelers to mainland China are advised to take precautions against mosquito bites. The outbreak demonstrates the ongoing threat of vector-borne diseases in the region.

Global health authorities are monitoring several viruses that could become the next public health threats. Researchers warn that canine coronavirus, which has been linked to human respiratory illness in Southeast Asia, and influenza D commonly found in cows deserve closer monitoring. These pathogens have pandemic potential and require continued surveillance. The scientific community emphasizes the importance of early detection and rapid response capabilities to prevent future outbreaks from becoming global health emergencies.

A new study on vaccine effectiveness in Hong Kong analyzed adverse events following vaccination with mRNA and inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccines. The retrospective study provides important safety data for public health decision-making. Despite vaccine hesitancy due to fear of adverse reactions, vaccination remains a cornerstone of pandemic control. The findings contribute to ongoing discussions about vaccine policy and booster shot recommendations for different population groups.

Public reaction to emerging disease threats varies based on trust in government and media coverage. During disease outbreaks, social media plays a dual role in both spreading information and misinformation. Studies show that clear, timely communication from health authorities improves public compliance with preventive measures. Fear and anxiety can lead to both appropriate precautions and panic buying or discrimination against affected communities. Understanding public response patterns is essential for effective crisis communication.

Hong Kong's Department of Health has prepared a comprehensive preparedness and response plan for novel infectious diseases. The plan encourages the public to adopt preventive measures such as observing good personal hygiene including washing hands properly and maintaining cough manners. Members of the public are advised to consult a doctor if they develop symptoms. The plan operates under the Prevention and Control of Disease Ordinance and includes guidelines for various outbreak scenarios. Regular drills and exercises ensure readiness for potential public health emergencies.

Researchers are exploring innovative approaches to antiviral drug discovery as preparation for potential future pandemics. Broad-spectrum antivirals that can treat multiple viruses simultaneously represent a significant research focus. Scientists have screened large databases of compounds and discovered novel inhibitors of various viruses. The development of drugs that can be rapidly deployed against newly emerged diseases is a priority. Investment in antiviral research has intensified in response to multiple viral threats including MERS, Zika, Ebola, and monkeypox.

The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reported updates on respiratory virus epidemiology, SARS-CoV-2 variants, mpox, leprosy, Marburg virus disease, dengue, and chikungunya in December 2025. Multiple disease threats require ongoing surveillance and coordination across countries. The report highlights the importance of international cooperation in disease monitoring and response. Health authorities are particularly concerned about the potential for cross-border spread of infectious diseases.

Hong Kong has seen a drastic increase in norovirus cases linked to raw oysters, with cases rising from about one per week in late December to 16 cases in the first five days of February. Health authorities have issued warnings about consuming raw or partially cooked bivalve shellfish. Pregnant women, young children, the elderly, and people with weakened immune systems are particularly advised to avoid raw oysters. The Centre for Health Protection is conducting epidemiological investigations and has advised restaurants to follow proper food handling procedures.

Public health experts emphasize that case detection, reporting, clear and timely dissemination of information, and strict infection control measures are essential in handling infectious disease outbreaks. The need for a dedicated outbreak response unit is crucial to combat any future outbreak. During the SARS outbreak in Hong Kong, these principles proved vital in controlling the spread. Healthcare facilities were identified as high-risk areas for transmission, requiring enhanced infection control protocols.
